namedutils: reject empty type and field names (#462)

`all()` returns True for the empty string, so an empty name passed both
ValueError checks in the validation loop and reached `name[0].isdigit()`,
raising IndexError instead of the intended ValueError. Both namedtuple and
namedlist were affected, for an empty field name and an empty typename.

The rename branch a few lines above already guards with `or not name`; add
the same guard to the validation loop and extend the message, which was
vacuously true for the empty string.

rows.commit_message:
Fix match_previous_expr to match nested and repeated expressions (#653)

copy_token_to_repeater added a new guard parse action to the repeated
expression on every match of the leading expression, and never removed
one. After N matches all N guards ran on each attempt to match, so at
most one could succeed. A second pair anywhere in the input failed, and
once a parse had failed the expression kept rejecting valid input.

Keep the pending matches on a stack instead, and register the guard once
at construction, so an inner match pairs with the nearest enclosing
match. Entries recorded at or after the current location are dropped, so
matches left behind by a backtracked branch cannot be paired.

Issue #560

rows.commit_message:
timeutils: scale isoparse fractional seconds to microseconds

isoparse parsed the fractional-second field as a literal integer, so
'.851' (e.g. from isoformat(timespec='milliseconds')) became 851
microseconds instead of 851000, silently corrupting round-trips the
docstring promises. Right-pad the fraction to six digits before
converting; leading zeros ('.051') scale correctly.

Deliberate behavior change: fractions with more than six digits
(nanosecond timestamps from Go services, databases, etc.) previously
raised ValueError from the datetime constructor; they now truncate to
microsecond precision, which matches what most ISO 8601 parsers do.
Pinned by test.

timeutils: guard daterange against non-advancing steps

daterange looped forever whenever the step could not make progress
toward stop. Reachable several ways: step=0, self-cancelling
month/day tuples like (0, 1, -31) (Jan 1 -> +1 month -> Feb 1 ->
-31 days -> Jan 1), and steps pointed away from stop (start < stop
with a negative step walks off unboundedly).

Replace input enumeration with a progress invariant: after each
advance, a stationary result raises ValueError (including
cancellations that only become stationary partway through a
sequence, e.g. (0, 1, -28) starting from Jan 1), and a step that
stops approaching stop terminates iteration. A step pointed away
from stop up front yields nothing, matching range(1, 5, -1).

Also covers datetime starts with sub-day timedelta steps (datetime
subclasses date), now pinned by test.

rows.commit_message:
Copy the occurrence lists when renumbering, not when copying

Copying them in copy() put the cost on the parse path: with packrat or
left-recursion enabled, copy() runs on every cache store and every cache hit,
and the dict comprehension cost ~90ns even when there are no results names at
all.

Only __delitem__ and insert renumber the recorded offsets, so let copy() keep
sharing the lists and have those two renumber a private copy instead.
__setitem__ and __iadd__ already build new lists.

Measured, 200k iterations each, best of five:

  copy() with 3 results names   311 -> 637 -> 323 ns
  copy() with no results names  277 -> 365 -> 276 ns
  insert()                     1192 -> 1173 -> 1548 ns
  del r[0]                     1626 -> 1581 -> 2067 ns

(unpatched -> copying in copy() -> copying when renumbering)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix get_timezone_gmt hour for negative fractional offsets (#1291)

For a timezone whose UTC offset has a non-zero minute part and is negative (e.g. America/St_Johns at UTC-03:30), get_timezone_gmt rendered the hour one step too far from zero, producing 'GMT-04:30' instead of 'GMT-03:30'.
